A1.justification: The PDFs describe successive versions of the same GFlowNet-composition work despite the changed title. Both versions are readable, including their figures, tables, equations and complete theoretical and experimental appendices.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix B report original grid and molecular-generation experiments, including distribution errors, reward, diversity, inference costs and molecular validity.

after.justification: V2 retains original grid and molecular experiments and reports additional method variants, temperature analyses, molecular ablations and Pareto-based evaluations.

M1.justification: V1 obtains reaching probabilities from explicitly learned state flows. V2 retains this route as Model F and adds DB F, which accumulates forward/backward policy ratios during generation (Section 4.1; Appendix A.2.3). This changes the inference procedure and enables composition of TB-trained models without an explicit state-flow model.

E1.justification: The grid, fragment-based molecular and QM9 domains and their base rewards remain. V2 adds directed binary contrast scenarios for fragment generation, including SEH subtract QED and QED subtract SA (Tables A6–A8). These extend the tested requirements for which properties must be suppressed beyond the corresponding three-objective contrasts in v1.

E2.justification: V2 evaluates OP-GFN in hypervolume, IGD+, Pareto Count and inference-cost comparisons; v1 only discussed the work. V2 also adds the ensemble comparator to the retained molecular tasks in Table A3, where v1 explicitly excluded it. MOGFN, HN-GFN and classifier guidance remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Pareto-based metrics, temperature-sensitivity protocols and TB/SubTB controls. Fragment scalarization changes from beta=64 to 32, and QM9 SA/QED bin thresholds change from 0.4 to 0.3. Appendix B also revises grid flow-network depth and classifier settings, including objective-matched two-/three-way classifiers and QM9 embedding dimension 128 to 64. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds molecular ablations isolating reaching-probability weighting across SubTB- and TB-trained models (Table A3), plus scalarization sensitivity and distortion analysis for beta=1,2,4 (Figure A7). Molecular-validity analysis expands to contrast operations. The earlier reward-correlation failure analysis is retained as Table A9 and Figure A8, with revised measurements.

E5.justification: V1 reports molecular point estimates without a stated seed count. V2 first reports means and standard deviations over three seeds for reward/diversity, Pareto metrics, logical target-bin percentages and validity, and labels full-bin distributions as three-seed means. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; it does not establish an increase from a known v1 run count.

E6.justification: Grid Tables 1–2 and A2 retain their values, but molecular results are extensively revised and DB F, Pareto-metric, ablation and temperature results are added. For example, three-objective QM9 validity changes from 54.8% for classifier guidance and 99.8% for ours (v1 Table 6) to 90.4±6.5%, 95.6±2.6% for Model F and 97.2±1.8% for DB F (v2 Table 7). These are revised evaluations, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2.3 adds the detailed-balance derivation of reaching probabilities as products of forward/backward policy ratios, assuming convergence. Appendix A.1 corrects N_M(s)=u_M(s) to N_M(s)=(sum_j omega_j Z_j)u_M(s). The principal linear-exactness theorem and L1-error decomposition otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The principal distributional guarantees and competitive-generation claims remain. V2 strengthens the abstract's characterization of baseline requirements to joint training and retraining from scratch when objectives change, while explicitly locating its own no-additional-training promise at composition time. Section 4.2 removes the explicit first-method novelty claim.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 removes v1's conjecture that classifier guidance steers generation into invalid regions. V2 instead interprets validity as close to base models and comparable to or better than classifier guidance. It also clarifies that incorporating a new objective requires training its base GFlowNet. The limitation caused by positively correlated rewards remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository pointer, fuller grid-baseline architecture descriptions and OP-GFN implementation information. It clarifies valid-sample bin reporting and the direction of the GAP reward. Conversely, it omits v1's molecular sampling temperature of 0.99, separate grid logZ learning rate and percentile-based GAP-scaling description. These omissions do not establish actual procedural changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ishibuchi et al. (2015) for IGD+, refines the description of order-preserving GFlowNets and explains their comparison through Pareto metrics. It also withdraws the explicit first-method priority claim. Most cited works and the broader research positioning remain; bibliographic corrections concern existing references.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title to Routing by Reaching, edits the abstract, introduction and discussion, subdivides Appendix A.2 into the two computational routes, and consolidates duplicated molecular implementation sections in Appendix B.2. Acknowledgements and proceedings information are added. The overall section sequence and much of the exposition remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds hypervolume Table 4, ablation and optimization Tables A3–A5, and temperature-analysis Figure A7. Molecular tables gain variant and uncertainty columns, with several widened across both columns. Separate classifier bin tables are merged into Table A8, and the correlation plot is redrawn as Figure A8. Most original grid figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation through three-seed uncertainty reporting, molecular weighting and training-objective ablations, nonlinear-temperature tests and Pareto-based comparisons. These address v1's missing variability estimates and limited molecular checks of the central weighting mechanism. The derived and tested DB F route also broadens supported base models, while the validity interpretation becomes more qualified. Some implementation details disappear and changed settings prevent direct performance comparisons, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger evidence and justified applicability.
